questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: it was crucial to me that the exchange was in a Spanish speaking country as i wanted to further my spanish skills but also the that the culture of the host city/university was interesting. Of course the academic level had to be sufficient also

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: every university is different and so is the culture and way of teaching, this can be hard to adapt to, something i would have wished for more information about during the host university selection process, you go into a lot of this with your eyes half closed, and a lot of information that would have been nice to have before the stay was not communicated to us prior to the arrival in the country.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: a little hard, not much was communicated to us, many only spoke Catalan, no english. the same for the university webpage some of the pages was not translated from catalan

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: there was an online call the week before the semester started where all exchange students could get the basic information, and ask if they had questions about anything

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: look at idealista, and dont stress about it many dont rent out far in advance,  i got my apartment two weeks before i was supposed to arrive in Barcelona, or look at "badi" if you are just looking for a room in an apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: look for apartments near the stations, and be aware that there is almost always changes/ delays in public transport in Barcelona, staying in the City instead of on campus gives you the opportunity to go partying and explore the city without having to catch the last train back to campus ( they don't drive all night)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: you went to the information desk and registered ad payed the insurance/registration fee of like 5 EUR of something like that

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: information desk you could go to physically or send an email

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% success got all the courses i registered for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: register for the courses you want on the day the registration opens, then you are sure to get it, it is "first come first served"

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the level is fine, it depends one the courses you take, some of them are a little back to basics, but some are the same as a normal alective course would have been at UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: the Teaching style is a bit more like highschool compared to UCPH you have classes, with a teacher with class assignments and projects you have to present to the class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Foreign(external) Trade 
Economic and management control
Marketing management 
Strategic management 
Economic policy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Strategic management, was a really good course, the teacher and structure of the classes was nice, i feel like a will remember what i have done in the class and be able to use it in my real life for more than just an exam. this actually aplies for most of my courses, apart from Economic policy, but that might be related to my interests.

questions.answer: none

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: food and everyday spendings are have a lower price, but you go out more to experience the city and area, so you use more money than you do in your home city

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: there was a lot

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
almost anything 
there is a gym faculty with the opportunity tho do almost any sport you can think of, and loads of social clubs for any interest

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
sign up for the sports faculty, it is cheap and you can go whenever you want wether it is between classes or after school. 

sign up for the free Catalan classes, helps you a little in your everyday life

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go to the smaller cities around the coast Erasmus and ESNUAB or ESNBarcelona has many weekend or day trips, find them on facebook. it is also a nice way to meet other exchange students.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: it was easy,

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: it can be hard as many of them are not the best at english but just through the social clubs and classes you will get to know some of them

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: i didn't find any of them challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the food and the nightlife, the fact that you can walk don to a park and there will be groups dancing Batchata or Salsa or another latin dance, and anyone is welcome to join or just look

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Start the process of getting your NIE number waay before you go to spain it takes a looong time
be prepared for people not speaking english 
it is very analogue - writing in hand at the exams and so on

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: all of the people i got to know and the experiences we had together.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: getting used to their way of teaching

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.answer: Yes
